# Why We're Changing How We Teach Maths

## What's Changing?

From next year, we're moving away from **streaming** (where students are separated into different classes based on ability) to **mixed-attainment teaching** (where students of different abilities learn together in the same class).

We know this might feel like a big change, so we want to explain why we're doing it.

---

## Why Make This Change?

### It helps more students do well

Research shows that when students learn together in mixed groups:
- Students who find maths harder don't fall further behind
- Students who are ahead don't get bored – they learn by explaining ideas to others
- Everyone benefits from hearing different ways of solving problems

### It's fairer

Streaming can lock students into a path early on. A child who struggles in Year 7 might stay in a lower stream for years, even if they improve. Mixed-attainment teaching gives every student the chance to progress.

### It builds confidence

When students only learn with others at the same level, some feel labelled as "not good at maths." Mixed groups help all students see themselves as capable mathematicians.

### Real-world maths doesn't separate by ability

In jobs and in life, people work together regardless of their strengths. Mixed teaching prepares students for this.

---

## What Will Actually Happen in the Classroom?

Your child won't just sit with 30 students doing the same worksheet. Instead:

- **Teachers will give different tasks** to different students based on what they need
- **Students will work in small groups** – sometimes with peers at similar levels, sometimes mixed
- **Everyone learns the same maths concepts**, but at a depth that suits them
- **Teachers will have more time** to spot who needs extra help

---

## What About My Child?

**If your child finds maths easy:**
- They'll still be challenged with harder problems
- They'll develop deeper understanding by explaining concepts to others
- They won't be held back

**If your child finds maths difficult:**
- They'll get targeted support from the teacher
- They won't feel separated or labelled
- They'll see that everyone struggles sometimes – and that's normal

**For all students:**
- Learning will be more personalised
- There will be more one-to-one teacher time available
- Progress will be tracked carefully

---

## What About Exam Results?

Schools using mixed-attainment teaching get strong results. Students don't fall behind – in fact, many do better because they're more confident and engaged.

---

## How Can You Help at Home?

- **Talk positively about maths** – avoid saying things like "I was never good at maths"
- **Encourage problem-solving** – maths is about thinking, not just getting the right answer
- **Ask your child to explain** how they solved something – this helps them learn
- **Stay in touch** – let us know if you have concerns

---

## Questions?

We're here to help. Please contact [teacher/department] if you'd like to discuss this further or have specific concerns about your child.
